006.brief:
Goal: identify anonymised PDF fonts (e.g. `CIDFont+F1`, no usable name table) by a glyph-width fingerprint, and use it in ranking and the analysis text.

- crates/engine/src/text_fonts.rs: `FontFile` (l.9-15, derives PartialEq; add a width field); `discover` (l.61-101) reads each face's bytes, so compute widths here for a fixed probe set (A–Z, a–z, Cyrillic А–я/Ё/ё, 0–9, common punctuation), normalised to 1000 em. `Wanted` (l.133-143) needs the PDF side's widths and a `from_facts` path (l.149). `Match` (l.205) and `rank` (l.228-256): add a fingerprint match between Exact (10_000) and Alias (6_000). Widths come from `pdfcraft_fonts::pdf::Metrics` (crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs l.31; `width(code)` l.720; `text_of(code)` l.755 for ToUnicode, `codes` l.693). Map each char to its code and width; only chars the font actually has.

030.title: Fix 2 failing UI tests: tools_panel_side_preference and use_system_title_bar (Preferences clicks have no effect)
030.brief:
`cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test ui` fails 2 of 51 on feature/0.2.6 (also at 4b6efea3 before task 027, so not caused by it):

031.title: Tab moved to another window: the source window must close, not stay on the start page
031.brief:
Regression (seen again in build 0.3.0, after tasks 010/029): when a tab is dragged into another window's tab strip, it joins the target, but the source window does NOT close; it stays open showing the empty start (title) page. Expected: if the moved tab was the last one in the source window, that window (or process, for tear-off windows) closes by itself; if other tabs remain, it simply keeps them.
Where: crates/ui-egui/src/tear_off.rs, doc_windows.rs (cross-process hand-off and the same-process path), possibly the ghost overlay from 029 keeping a viewport/drag state alive.
Do: reproduce with a test (same-process and cross-process hand-off paths), find why the close is skipped, fix, add regression tests that assert the source window closes after its last tab left and survives with remaining tabs. Cover the abort cases (drop refused, target gone: tab must come back, window must NOT close then). Never-panic rules. Done when fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui are green; describe a manual check in the report.

Where: crates/ui-egui/src/print_ui.rs and the print settings/state/default + persisted Preferences (a saved old value 'portrait' from earlier versions must not pin it: if the stored value was never chosen explicitly by the user, treat as Automatic; check how settings are stored and migrate sensibly). 033.title: Text edit field: preview of a substituted font differs from the final result and the original
033.brief:
Still wrong after task 027 (build 0.3.0): when the original font is replaced by a substitute (not embedded / not installed), the text shown in the in-place edit field (preview while typing) looks different from (a) the final rendering after the edit is committed and (b) the original font. Expected: the preview uses exactly the same font face, weight, style, size, letter/word widths and line wrapping as the committed result, and the substitute is the closest metric-compatible match to the original (glyph widths, see tasks 004/006/027).
Where: crates/ui-egui (edit_text_ui, canvas, text_panel, fonts/text_fonts), the engine side that renders the committed text. Find the divergence: probably the egui editor uses a different font family/fallback chain than the engine's final render. Make both go through one font-resolution function. Add tests that the resolved face for a given (original font name, flags) is identical for preview and commit, and a metric test on widths. Use the PDFs available in the repo test fixtures; if a table-like PDF with Cyrillic text is available, use it. Never use fonts from Adobe or installed system fonts for embedding (AGENTS.md). Done when fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test (touched crates) are green; describe a manual check.

034.title: Edit PDF: separate fields get merged into one text block (e.g. 'Доступ к сети Московского офиса' and 'Пользователь')
034.brief:
Bug in build 0.3.0: in the user's PDF АнисимовИГ.pdf (a form/table; the file is not in the repo - the user has it, so work from fixtures and synthetic PDFs), some separate fields, e.g. 'Доступ к сети Московского офиса' and 'Пользователь', are joined into ONE editable text block in Edit PDF. Each visually separate label/cell must be its own block.
Where: text block grouping/segmentation in the engine and ui-egui (look at line/paragraph merging in the text extraction used by Edit PDF; tasks 014/015 touched the wrap boundary and the 0.9.0 sync tasks 022 ported the upstream grouping). Find which heuristic merges them (likely a horizontal-gap or baseline tolerance too loose, or same-line merge across columns/table cells, large gaps, different fonts/size, a ruling line or cell border between them). Fix: do not merge text runs across a large horizontal gap (relative to font size), across different cells/columns, or across vector lines/borders; keep normal paragraphs and wrapped lines merged. Build a synthetic test PDF (two labels on one baseline with a wide gap, and a table-cell layout) and regression tests asserting separate blocks, plus tests that ordinary multi-line paragraphs still merge. Check for regression of tasks 014/015. Done when fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test (touched crates) are green.

035.title: Flaky ui-egui tests on Windows: d3d10warp.dll access violation when wgpu tests run in parallel
035.brief:
Finding: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test content` (and probably other egui_kittest+wgpu test binaries) crashes about 1 run in 6 on Windows with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005); Windows Application log (event 1000) names the faulting module d3d10warp.dll (Windows WARP software rasterizer, driven by wgpu). Each crashing test passes alone (15/15) and with --test-threads=1 (14/14): it is a race when several tests create/use a wgpu D3D device in parallel threads. Not our code (unsafe_code is forbidden), but it makes cargo test and CI red at random and stops `cargo test --workspace` at the first crashed binary.
Goal: make this deterministic without hiding real failures. Options, pick the least invasive and verify: (a) a shared test helper that serialises creation/use of the kittest wgpu harness behind one global Mutex (poison-tolerant) used by all ui-egui test binaries; (b) a harness config that renders without wgpu where the test needs no pixels (egui_kittest without wgpu for logic tests, wgpu only for snapshot tests); (c) per-crate test-threads limit through .cargo/config.toml - last resort, as it slows all tests and does not cover CI. Check .github workflows too (the CI runner for Windows must benefit as well).
Done when: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` passes 10 times in a row on this Windows machine with default threads (script it, report counts), fmt and clippy -D warnings are green, and the report states which option was used and the before/after crash rate.
